c01: The soul ascends through the *heikhalot* (heavenly palaces) by means of mystical prayer and secret names to behold the *Merkavah* (Divine Chariot) and the glory of the *Ein Sof*.
The traveler traverses the *maqamat* (stations) of the *nafs* (soul) through *mi'raj* (ascension) until the heart is annihilated in the *fana* of the Divine Presence, reaching the ultimate *baqa*.
Through the cultivation of *qi* and the refinement of the *dan tian*, the practitioner achieves *xian* (immortality) and ascends to merge with the *Dao*, the primordial source of all existence.

The practitioner transcends the *samsaric* realms through *dhyana* (meditation) and the realization of *sunyata* (emptiness), ultimately attaining *nirvana*, the cessation of suffering and the liberation of the enlightened mind.

Through the practice of *yoga* and the awakening of *kundalini*, the *atman* (individual soul) ascends through the *chakras* to realize its essential unity with *Brahman*, the supreme, undifferentiated reality.

By the grace of God and the imitation of Christ, the soul undergoes *theosis* (divinization), ascending through prayer and contemplation to participate eternally in the beatific vision of the Holy Trinity.
The soul sheds its planetary garments as it ascends through the *spheres* of the *cosmos*, seeking to reunite its *pneuma* with the *Monad* through the transformative work of the Great Art.

Through the exercise of *nous* (intellect) and the practice of *theoria* (contemplation), the soul ascends from the sensible world to contemplate the *Form of the Good*, the ultimate source of all truth.
c02: The *Ein Sof* emanates the *Ayin*, the primordial nothingness from which the *Reshimu* or divine residue forms the foundation of all created existence.
The *al-Haqq* manifests the *al-Jawhar al-Fard*, the indivisible substance or subtle essence that serves as the underlying reality of all contingent forms.
The *Wuji*, the ultimate nothingness, gives rise to the *Taiji*, the supreme polarity that acts as the generative source of all ten thousand things.
All phenomena arise from *Sunyata*, the emptiness that is not a substance but the interdependent nature of reality from which all forms momentarily emerge.
The *Prakriti*, the primordial nature or undifferentiated matter, evolves into the manifest universe through the interaction of the three *gunas* under the influence of *Purusha*.
God created the world *ex nihilo*, bringing forth the *materia prima* as the formless potentiality that receives the divine imprint of order and being.
The *prima materia*, or *hyle*, is the chaotic, unformed base of the Great Work, containing the hidden seed of the Philosopher’s Stone within its dark, mercurial depths.
The *arche*, the fundamental principle or source, is the underlying substrate from which all things are composed and to which they ultimately return in the cycle of nature.
c03: All things are but vessels of *Ein Sof*, possessing no independent essence, for they exist only as manifestations of the Divine Will that sustains them from moment to moment.
All things are *fana* in the face of the Divine, for they possess no *wujud* of their own, existing only as fleeting reflections of the Absolute Reality, *al-Haqq*.
All things arise from the *Dao* and return to it, for they lack a fixed *ziran* and exist only as shifting, interdependent transformations within the vast, spontaneous flow of the *wanwu*.
All phenomena are marked by *sunyata*, lacking any *svabhava* or inherent existence, as they arise dependently through the complex web of *pratityasamutpada* without a permanent, unchanging core.
All forms are *maya*, lacking *atman* or independent reality, for they are merely transient appearances superimposed upon the singular, unchanging *Brahman* through the play of cosmic ignorance.
All creatures are *ex nihilo* and possess no being of their own, for they are entirely contingent upon the sustaining grace of God, in whom alone true *esse* resides.
All things are but shadows of the *Monad*, possessing no fixed nature, for they are in constant flux, reflecting the hidden *prima materia* that underlies the shifting veil of manifestation.
All things are in a state of *panta rhei*, possessing no *ousia* that is not subject to change, for they are merely transient configurations of matter within the eternal, shifting cosmos.
c04: The highest good is to cleave to the Divine through the observance of *mitzvot*, thereby achieving *devekut* and fulfilling one’s purpose as a vessel for the manifestation of the *Ein Sof*.
True flourishing is found in *taqwa*, the God-conscious surrender of the self to the Divine Will, which leads the soul to *fana* and the ultimate realization of *tawhid* in the Beloved.

To live well is to cultivate *de* (virtue) through the practice of *li* (ritual propriety) and *ren* (humaneness), thereby aligning one’s life with the natural flow and transformative power of the *Dao*.
The highest good is the cessation of *dukkha* through the realization of *anatta* and the cultivation of *panna*, leading to the ultimate liberation of *Nirvana* from the cycle of *samsara*.

True flourishing is the attainment of *moksha* by fulfilling one’s *dharma* and realizing the identity of the individual *atman* with the ultimate reality of *Brahman*, transcending the illusions of *maya*.
The highest good is the *beatific vision*, where the soul finds its true end in the *summum bonum* of union with God through *caritas* and the grace of the Holy Spirit.

The goal of life is the *magnum opus* of spiritual transmutation, whereby the seeker achieves *gnosis* and the alchemical marriage of opposites, reflecting the macrocosmic harmony of *as above, so below*.
The highest good is *eudaimonia*, achieved through the exercise of *arete* (virtue) and the cultivation of *phronesis* (practical wisdom) in accordance with the rational order of the *logos*.
c05: The soul seeks *devekut*, a cleaving to the Ein Sof, where the individual ego is utterly nullified and absorbed into the infinite radiance of the Divine Presence.
Through *fana*, the traveler undergoes the annihilation of the self, passing away from the illusions of the ego to subsist eternally in the reality of *baqa* with the Beloved.
By practicing *zuowang* or "sitting in forgetfulness," one discards the body and intelligence to merge with the *Dao*, returning to the primordial state of non-being and spontaneous naturalness.
Through the realization of *anatta*, the practitioner extinguishes the fires of craving and ignorance, attaining *nirvana* as the illusory construct of a permanent self dissolves into emptiness.
The seeker achieves *moksha* when the individual *atman* realizes its essential identity with *Brahman*, dissolving the veil of *maya* and ending the cycle of rebirth in absolute unity.
In the state of *unio mystica*, the soul is so consumed by the fire of divine love that it loses its own will, becoming one spirit with God in Christ.
The alchemist achieves the *coniunctio* of opposites, whereby the base self is calcined and purified until the soul is transmuted into the divine light of the *monad*.
The soul strives for *henosis*, a transcendent return to the One, where the intellect transcends discursive thought to become unified with the supreme, simple source of all existence.
c06: The *malakhim* serve as celestial messengers and intermediaries, traversing the bridge between the Infinite *Ein Sof* and the realm of humanity to execute the divine will.
The *mala'ika* are luminous beings created from light who act as intermediaries, conveying the divine commands of Allah to the hearts and affairs of humankind.
The *shen* are the numinous spirits and ancestral forces that mediate the flow of *qi* between the transcendent *Tian* and the earthly order of human society.
The *devas* inhabit the higher celestial realms, existing as sentient beings who, while subject to *samsara*, often serve as guardians or guides for those seeking the path to enlightenment.
The *devas* and *gandharvas* dwell in the intermediate spheres, acting as divine agents who bridge the vast expanse between the supreme *Brahman* and the mortal world of *karma*.
The holy angels are ministering spirits sent forth by God to serve as intermediaries, bridging the gap between the divine majesty of Heaven and the salvation of mankind.
The *daimones* or planetary intelligences act as the vital links in the *scala naturae*, mediating the influx of celestial power from the divine source down to the material world.
The *daimones* are intermediate beings who inhabit the space between the moon and earth, serving as messengers that convey the prayers of men to the gods and divine decrees to mortals.
c07: Man is the *Adam ha-Rishon*, a microcosm reflecting the *Sefirot* of the divine structure, containing within his soul the entire architecture of the upper and lower worlds.
The human being is the *al-insān al-kāmil*, the Perfect Man, who serves as the mirror in which the divine attributes of the macrocosm are fully reflected and realized.
The human body is a miniature *tianxia*, where the internal *qi* and organs correspond precisely to the cosmic order of Heaven and Earth, maintaining the harmony of the *Dao*.

While denying a permanent self, the tradition teaches that the human mind contains the *tathāgatagarbha*, a seed of enlightenment that encompasses the totality of all phenomena within the interconnected web of existence.
The individual *ātman* is identical to the universal *Brahman*, for the human body is a *piṇḍa* that mirrors the entire *brahmāṇḍa*, containing all worlds and deities within its subtle form.
Created in the *imago Dei*, man is a microcosm who recapitulates the order of creation, serving as the bridge between the material world and the spiritual realm of the Creator.
As it is written in the *Emerald Tablet*, that which is below is as that which is above, for man is the *microcosmos* reflecting the perfection of the *macrocosmos*.
Man is a *mikros kosmos*, a rational being whose soul is structured according to the same mathematical and harmonic proportions that govern the movement of the celestial spheres.
c08: The *Ein Sof* is the Infinite, utterly transcending all human language, attributes, or conceptual definitions, for it is the hidden root that precedes all manifestation and naming.
The *Al-Haqq* is beyond all names and attributes, for the Essence (*Dhat*) is veiled from the intellect and remains utterly transcendent, incomparable, and beyond the reach of human description.
The *Dao* that can be spoken is not the eternal *Dao*, for the nameless origin of heaven and earth transcends all categories and linguistic attempts to define its subtle, formless nature.

The ultimate reality is *Sunyata*, or emptiness, which transcends all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*) and cannot be captured by names, signs, or linguistic designations, as it is devoid of inherent existence.
The supreme *Brahman* is *Nirguna*, without qualities or attributes, and is described by the sages as *neti, neti*—not this, not that—for it lies beyond all speech and mental conceptualization.
God is the *hyperousios* or super-essential One, who dwells in the "dazzling darkness" of unknowing, transcending every name, affirmation, and negation that the human mind might attempt to impose.
The *Monad* is the ineffable source, the silent One that precedes all duality and cannot be grasped by the intellect, for it is the hidden light beyond all names and forms.
The *Hen* or the One is the ineffable principle beyond all being and discourse, which cannot be named or described, as it transcends the reach of both intellect and language.
c09: The *Ein Sof* emanates an infinite, primordial *Or* that permeates all creation, serving as the hidden essence of both the divine unity and the soul’s intellectual spark.
The *Nur* of Allah is the light of the heavens and the earth, illuminating the *qalb* of the seeker until the mirror of the mind reflects the Divine Presence.
The *Dao* is the subtle, luminous source of all things, and the sage cultivates an inner *de* that mirrors this celestial clarity within the stillness of the mind.
The *citta-prakrti* is naturally luminous, and when the defilements of ignorance are cleared, the mind realizes its own *prabhasvara* nature, which is the essence of enlightened awareness.
The *Atman* is the self-luminous *jyotir* that dwells within the heart, identical to the supreme *Brahman*, the singular light that reveals both the cosmos and the witnessing consciousness.
God is light, and in His light we see light, for the *Logos* illuminates every person, drawing the soul toward the beatific vision of the uncreated divine radiance.
The *Lux* of the Monad descends through the spheres to become the *lumen* of the human intellect, enabling the soul to recognize its own divine origin through gnosis.
The *noûs* is akin to the sun, for just as the sun grants visibility to objects, the Good grants truth and intelligibility to the mind’s rational faculty.
c10: From the hidden *Ein Sof*, the *Sefirot* emanate as vessels of divine light, unfolding the multiplicity of creation while remaining rooted in the absolute unity of the *Ayin*.
Through the *tajalli* of the Divine Essence, the *Wahdat al-Wujud* manifests as the infinite multiplicity of the cosmos, yet all things remain reflections of the One, *al-Haqq*.
The *Dao* gives birth to the One, the One to the two, the two to the three, and the three to the ten thousand things, which return to the *Wu* in stillness.

All phenomena arise from the *Dharmakaya* as interdependent manifestations of *Sunyata*, lacking inherent existence and appearing only through the beginningless play of *pratityasamutpada* or dependent origination.
From the singular *Brahman*, the entire universe of *maya* projects forth as a manifold appearance, yet the *Atman* remains identical to the ultimate, non-dual reality of the One.
By the *Logos*, through whom all things were made, the multiplicity of creation proceeds from the Father, reflecting the divine goodness in a hierarchy of being that seeks return to God.
As the *Monad* expands into the *Dyad* and the *Triad*, the *Prisca Theologia* reveals that all things emanate from the One, mirroring the celestial order in the terrestrial realm below.
From the *Hen*, the first principle, all beings emanate by a process of necessary overflow, like light from the sun, descending through levels of reality until reaching the limits of matter.
c12: Through the process of *gilgul neshamot*, the soul undergoes transmigration, entering new vessels until it achieves its ultimate rectification and returns to the source of all light.
The soul experiences *tanasukh*, a cycle of shifting forms, as it journeys through various states of existence to refine its essence before returning to the Divine Presence.
The *hun* and *po* souls disperse at death, yet the vital spirit may undergo *lunhui*, a cycle of transformation, reflecting the natural patterns of the Dao’s eternal unfolding.
Driven by *karma*, the stream of consciousness undergoes *punarbhava*, a rebirth into new forms of suffering or liberation, until the cessation of craving leads to the peace of *Nirvana*.
As a person casts off worn-out garments and puts on others that are new, the *atman* discards the exhausted body to enter a new one through the cycle of *samsara*.

While mainstream theology emphasizes the resurrection of the body, certain esoteric traditions contemplate the soul’s purification through successive earthly lives, a concept often termed *metempsychosis* or spiritual evolution.

The soul, a spark of the Divine, descends into the material realm and undergoes *metempsychosis*, passing through various incarnations to purge its impurities and ascend back to the celestial spheres.
The soul, being immortal and divine, undergoes *metempsychosis*, migrating from one body to another as it is purified through successive lives in accordance with the cosmic order of the universe.
c13: One must practice *bittul ha-yesh*, the nullification of the ego, surrendering one’s own will entirely to the divine *Ratzon* so that the soul becomes a transparent vessel for God’s light.
Through *fana*, the annihilation of the self, the seeker abandons their own limited will to become a mirror reflecting only the eternal *Haqq*, acting solely through the movement of the Divine.

By practicing *wu wei*, the sage aligns with the *Dao*, acting without artificial striving or personal agenda, allowing the natural order to unfold spontaneously through effortless, non-coercive activity.
By realizing *anatta*, the absence of a permanent self, one ceases the grasping of *tanha*, acting with *upekkha* (equanimity) so that deeds arise from wisdom rather than the delusions of ego.
Through *nishkama karma*, the performance of duty without attachment to the fruits of action, the seeker offers all deeds as a sacrifice to the Divine, transcending the bondage of personal desire.
One must practice *gelassenheit*, a holy yielding of the spirit, whereby the soul empties itself of its own will to become a passive instrument for the indwelling grace of God.
By achieving the *alchemical marriage* of the soul, the adept dissolves the ego in the *prima materia*, allowing the divine *Logos* to operate through them without the interference of human will.
Following the path of *apatheia*, the sage aligns their internal reason with the *Logos* of the cosmos, accepting all events with equanimity and acting in accordance with nature’s rational necessity.
c14: The *lev* (heart) serves as the vessel for *binah* (understanding), where the divine light of the *Ein Sof* is internalized and transformed into true spiritual wisdom.
The *qalb* (heart) is the subtle organ of *ma‘rifa* (gnosis), which, when polished of worldly attachments, becomes the mirror reflecting the divine realities of the *Haqq*.
The *xin* (heart-mind) is the seat of *de* (virtue) and the locus of intuitive resonance, where the sage aligns their inner nature with the unfolding of the *Dao*.
The *citta* (mind-heart) is the foundation of consciousness, which, when purified of *kleshas* (defilements), realizes the luminous nature of *prajna* (wisdom) and the emptiness of all phenomena.
The *hridaya* (heart-space) is the secret dwelling of the *Atman*, where the seeker attains *jnana* (knowledge) by realizing the identity of the individual self with the ultimate *Brahman*.
The heart is the inner sanctuary where the soul, through the grace of the Holy Spirit, attains the *theoria* (contemplation) of God and the illumination of divine truth.
The heart acts as the *athanor* of the soul, where the *lumen naturae* (light of nature) transmutes base ignorance into the golden wisdom of the *prisca sapientia*.
The heart is the *hegemonikon* (ruling faculty) of the soul, which, when governed by *logos* (reason), perceives the rational order and divine harmony of the cosmos.
c15: Through the *Otiyot* (letters) of the *Torah*, the Holy One, blessed be He, emanated the cosmos, for the *Dibbur* (divine word) is the primordial instrument of all creation.
By the command *Kun* (Be!), Allah brought the entire universe into existence, manifesting the hidden realities of the *al-Qalam* (Pen) through the eternal, creative power of His divine Word.
The *Dao* (Way) remains nameless and silent, yet it gives rise to the *Wanwu* (ten thousand things) through the spontaneous, generative resonance of its own inherent, unmanifested nature.

All phenomena arise as *dharmas* from the emptiness of *sunyata*, manifesting through the vibration of the primordial *mantra* or the transformative power of the *dharani* that sustains the illusory world.

The universe unfolds from the eternal *Om*, the primordial *nada* (sound) or *vak* (speech), through which the *Brahman* manifests the multiplicity of existence as a vibration of divine consciousness.
In the beginning was the *Logos*, and the Word was with God, and by this divine utterance all things were made, reflecting the creative power of the Father through the Son.
By the *Fiat Lux* of the Great Architect, the *Verbum* resonates through the elemental spheres, binding the macrocosm and microcosm together through the secret, vibratory power of the sacred Name.

The *Logos* acts as the rational, ordering principle of the *kosmos*, serving as the divine intelligence that articulates the formless matter into the harmonious structure of the intelligible universe.
c17: The soul ascends through the *Sefirot*, refining its *middot* to achieve *devekut*, a state of cleaving to the Divine Presence through the study of Torah and the performance of *mitzvot*.

The seeker traverses the *maqamat* (stations) and *ahwal* (states) of the *tariqa* (path), purifying the heart through *dhikr* to attain *fana* (annihilation) and *baqa* (subsistence) in the Divine Reality.
One cultivates the *Dao* by refining the *qi* through *wu wei* (non-action) and inner stillness, progressing from the natural state to the sage’s harmony with the spontaneous order of the universe.

The practitioner follows the *magga* of the Noble Eightfold Path, progressing through the stages of *sila* (morality), *samadhi* (concentration), and *panna* (wisdom) to achieve the ultimate liberation of *Nirvana*.
Through the practice of *yoga* and the discipline of *dharma*, the soul ascends the *marga* of devotion, knowledge, or action to realize *moksha*, the liberation of the *atman* into the Absolute.
The soul undergoes the three-fold way of purgation, illumination, and union, advancing through prayer and grace toward the *theosis* that restores the divine image within the human person.

The alchemist undergoes the *magnum opus*, transmuting the base metals of the soul through the stages of *nigredo*, *albedo*, and *rubedo* to achieve the spiritual perfection of the Philosopher’s Stone.
The philosopher practices *askesis* to purify the soul, ascending from the shadows of the material world through the exercise of *logos* and virtue to contemplate the eternal Forms of the Good.
c22: By contemplating the *Neshama* within, the soul ascends to perceive the *Ein Sof*, for the human image is a mirror reflecting the hidden mysteries of the *Sefirot*.
He who knows his own *nafs* (self) truly knows his *Rabb* (Lord), for the heart is the throne where the *tajalli* (divine manifestation) of the Beloved is witnessed.
To return to the *Dao* is to realize one’s *xing* (innate nature), for the sage who looks within finds the *Tian* (Heaven) already dwelling in the stillness of the heart.
By realizing the emptiness of the *atman* (self), one awakens to the *Buddha-nature* inherent within, transcending the illusions of *samsara* to perceive the ultimate reality of *Dharmakaya*.
When the *jiva* (individual soul) pierces the veil of *maya*, it recognizes its identity with *Brahman*, realizing that the *Atman* within is identical to the supreme *Paramatman*.
As the *imago Dei* restored by grace, the soul finds that by entering the inner sanctuary of the heart, it encounters the indwelling presence of the Triune God.
As above, so below: by transmuting the leaden self into the golden *Anthropos*, the adept realizes the *Microcosm* is the perfect mirror of the *Macrocosm* and the divine *Monad*.
By practicing the Delphic *gnothi seauton*, the philosopher ascends through reason to contemplate the *Logos*, recognizing that the rational soul is a spark of the divine *Nous*.
c23: Through *tishuvah* and *ta'anit*, the soul is refined and the *yetzer hara* subdued, allowing the sparks of holiness to ascend and reunite with the Divine *Ein Sof*.
By means of *sawm* and *mujahadat al-nafs*, the believer purifies the heart of worldly attachments, polishing the mirror of the soul to reflect the light of *al-Haqq*.
Through *zhai* (fasting) and the cultivation of *xin* (heart-mind), one achieves the stillness necessary to harmonize with the *Dao* and preserve the integrity of one’s *qi*.
By practicing *dhuta* (ascetic austerities) and *sila* (virtue), the practitioner purifies the mind of *kleshas*, weakening the fetters of craving to attain the clarity required for *nibbana*.
Through *tapas* (ascetic heat) and *upavasa* (fasting), the seeker burns away the impurities of *karma*, refining the *atman* to realize its essential unity with *Brahman*.
Through the discipline of fasting and *mortificatio*, the faithful soul subdues the flesh to purge the stain of sin, preparing the vessel to receive the sanctifying grace of the Holy Spirit.
By the *purificatio* of the material body, the alchemist dissolves the *prima materia* of the soul, stripping away base impurities to reveal the hidden *lumen naturae* within.

Through *askēsis* and the moderation of bodily appetites, the philosopher purifies the soul of irrational passions, achieving the *apatheia* necessary for the intellect to contemplate the eternal Forms.
c24: The four *yesodot* (elements) are but garments of the *Ein Sof*, constantly transmuting through the divine *sefirot* as they return to their primordial unity in the hidden light.
All *‘anāṣir* (elements) are manifestations of the Divine Names, perpetually undergoing *tajallī* (theophany) as they dissolve and reform within the infinite flux of the *‘ālam al-mithāl*.
The *wuxing* (five phases) undergo constant *bianhua* (transformation), cycling through the interaction of *yin* and *yang* to maintain the harmonious flow of the *Dao* throughout the myriad things.
The *mahabhuta* (great elements) are devoid of inherent existence, arising and ceasing in a continuous stream of *dharmas* governed by the law of *pratītyasamutpāda* (dependent origination).
The *panchabhuta* (five elements) emerge from *prakriti* and dissolve back into it, manifesting the eternal play of *guna* (qualities) within the cyclical unfolding of *samsara*.
The four elements are corruptible creatures sustained by the Word, which orders their constant transmutation to reflect the divine providence governing the temporal world.
Through the *magnum opus*, the *prima materia* is purified and transmuted, as the elements undergo *solutio* and *coagulatio* to achieve the perfection of the *lapis philosophorum*.
The four *stoicheia* (elements) are subject to constant *metabole* (change), as their qualities shift through the interaction of heat, cold, dryness, and moisture within the sublunary sphere.
c25: Through the *halom*, the Holy One communicates hidden mysteries to the soul, for a dream is one-sixtieth of prophecy, revealing the *sod* of the divine will to the waking heart.
The *ru’ya* is a fragment of *nubuwwa*, wherein the *qalb* perceives the *malakut* and receives true guidance from the Unseen, provided the seeker’s spirit is purified of worldly distractions.
The *meng* reflects the movement of the *qi* and the resonance of the *dao*, serving as a mirror where the sage discerns the patterns of Heaven and the state of his own *xin*.
As a *svapna* arising from the storehouse consciousness, the dream is an illusory manifestation of *karma*, yet the awakened mind may use it to perceive the emptiness of all conditioned phenomena.
The *svapna* state is a gateway where the *atman* experiences subtle realities, revealing the nature of *maya* and the deeper truths of the *Vedas* to the one who practices *yoga*.
God speaks to His servants in *visio*, granting divine revelation through the medium of dreams to instruct the faithful, warn the sinner, and manifest the mysteries of His holy providence.
In the *somnium*, the soul ascends to the celestial spheres, receiving *gnosis* and alchemical illumination as the *anima* is liberated from the heavy chains of the material body during sleep.
The *oneiros* is a divine messenger, a *theopemptos*, which provides the soul with glimpses of truth and future events, reflecting the rational order of the cosmos to the receptive mind.
c26: Upon the separation of the soul from the body, the *neshamah* ascends to the *Olam Ha-Ba* to stand before the Heavenly Court, where its deeds are weighed in the balance of divine justice.
After the *barzakh*, the soul faces the questioning of Munkar and Nakir, awaiting the Day of Judgment when Allah weighs the *mizan* of one’s deeds to determine entry into Paradise or Hell.
The soul’s *hun* spirit ascends to the celestial realm while the *po* descends to the earth, where the Ten Kings of Hell preside over the judgment of one’s earthly conduct and karmic debts.

Driven by *karma*, the consciousness undergoes *punarbhava*, transmigrating through the six realms of existence until the cessation of craving allows the liberated mind to attain the peace of *Nirvana*.

The *atman* sheds the physical body like worn garments, passing before *Yamaraja* to receive the fruits of its *karma*, eventually transmigrating into a new form until the realization of *moksha* is achieved.
At the moment of death, the soul undergoes the Particular Judgment, appearing before Christ to account for its earthly life, awaiting the final resurrection and the eternal destiny of Heaven or Hell.
The soul, having shed its planetary garments, ascends through the celestial spheres to be weighed in the balance of the *Logos*, seeking purification and union with the Divine *Nous* or *Monad*.
The soul, freed from the prison of the body, descends to the underworld to be judged by Minos, Rhadamanthus, and Aeacus, who assign it to the appropriate place of punishment or blessed repose.
c28: The *Shekhinah* (Divine Presence) is hidden within all created things, and the sparks of holiness, the *nitzotzot*, are scattered throughout the entirety of the manifest world.
The *Haqq* (Truth) is closer to man than his own jugular vein, for the *Nur* (Light) of Allah permeates the hidden depths of every human heart.
The *Dao* (Way) flows through all things, and the *de* (virtue/inner power) manifests the ultimate reality within the nature of every being.
All beings possess the *Tathāgatagarbha* (Buddha-nature), an inherent, luminous potential for awakening that remains present even when obscured by the *kleshas* (afflictions) of the mind.
The *Ātman* (Self) is identical to *Brahman* (the Absolute), dwelling within the lotus of the heart as the eternal, unchanging witness of every living being.
We are temples of the Holy Spirit, for the *Imago Dei* (Image of God) is imprinted upon the soul, allowing the indwelling Christ to live within the faithful.
As above, so below; the *Monad* reflects itself in every part of the *Macrocosm*, for the divine *Pneuma* animates the secret essence of all created things.
The *Logos* (Divine Reason) permeates the entire cosmos, acting as the rational spark that connects the soul of every human being to the governing intelligence of the universe.
c29: What is hateful to you, do not do to your neighbor; this is the whole Torah, while the rest is commentary, for all are created in the image of the Divine.
None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself, reflecting the mercy of Allah, the Compassionate, toward all His creation.
Do not impose on others what you yourself do not desire, for the practice of *ren* (humaneness) and the harmony of the *Dao* require treating all beings with reciprocal care.
Considering others as oneself, one should neither kill nor cause to kill, practicing *karuna* (compassion) for all sentient beings to alleviate the universal suffering of *samsara*.
One should never do to another what one would regard as injurious to one's own self; this is the essence of *dharma*, the path of righteousness toward all living beings.
In everything, do to others what you would have them do to you, for this sums up the Law and the Prophets, reflecting the command to love your neighbor as yourself.
As above, so below; treat all living things with the sacred reverence due to the microcosm, for the *Anima Mundi* binds all beings in a single, divine, and interconnected chain of existence.
Do not do to others what you would be angry if they did to you, for the *oikeiosis* of the wise recognizes that all rational beings share in the universal law of nature.
c31: The lower worlds are a reflection of the upper *Sefirot*, for all that exists in the *Olam ha-Zeh* is patterned after the divine structure of the *Olam ha-Atzilut*.
The manifest world is a mirror of the Divine Names, for every *zahir* (outward form) in the created realm corresponds to a *batin* (inward reality) within the *‘Alam al-Mithal*.
The *Tian* (Heaven) and the *Di* (Earth) form a single resonant system, where the *li* (principle) of the cosmos is mirrored in the moral and natural order of the human realm.

All phenomena are empty of inherent existence, yet they arise through *pratitya-samutpada* (dependent origination), where the macrocosm of the universe is reflected within the microcosm of the sentient mind.
The *brahmanda* (macrocosm) is identical to the *pinda* (microcosm), for the *atman* (self) within the individual is fundamentally one with the *Brahman* that pervades the entire cosmic order.
As the *Imago Dei*, man is a microcosm reflecting the divine order, for the visible creation serves as a *speculum* revealing the invisible perfections and eternal power of the Creator.
As it is written in the *Emerald Tablet*, that which is below is like that which is above, and that which is above is like that which is below, to accomplish the miracles.
The cosmos is a single living organism governed by *sympatheia*, where the movements of the celestial spheres exert a causal influence upon the terrestrial realm through the chain of *logos*.
c32: Through *hitbodedut*, the soul withdraws from the clamor of the material world into the profound silence of *ayin*, where the divine light of *Ein Sof* may be perceived in stillness.
By practicing *muraqaba*, the seeker stills the heart’s agitation, for in the silence of the *nafs*, the mirror of the soul reflects the unveiling of the Divine Truth, *al-Haqq*.
By cultivating *wu-wei* and emptying the heart-mind of worldly desires, one returns to the primordial *pu*, where the stillness of the *Dao* reveals the natural order of all things.
Through the practice of *samatha*, the mind is brought to a state of perfect stillness, allowing the light of *prajna* to pierce the illusions of *samsara* and realize *nirvana*.
When the fluctuations of the *citta* are stilled through *dhyana*, the veil of *maya* lifts, and the *atman* rests in the silent, luminous realization of its identity with *Brahman*.
In the holy silence of *hesychia*, the soul descends from the intellect into the heart, where, stripped of all images, it waits in stillness to be united with the Divine Word.
By the *magnum silentium* of the inner laboratory, the alchemist stills the volatile elements of the soul, allowing the *lumen naturae* to distill the hidden truth of the Philosopher’s Stone.
Through the *ataraxia* of the soul, the philosopher achieves a state of undisturbed stillness, enabling the intellect to contemplate the eternal, unchanging forms of the *Logos* in perfect clarity.
c33: In the beginning, the Ein Sof contracted its infinite light through the process of Tzimtzum to create a void, allowing the emanations of the Sefirot to bring forth the manifest worlds.
Allah brought the universe into existence through the command "Kun!" (Be!), manifesting the hidden treasures of His essence into the multiplicity of the seen and unseen realms of creation.
Before heaven and earth existed, the nameless Dao flowed as the primordial unity, giving birth to the One, then the Two, and finally the ten thousand things through the movement of Qi.

The universe arises not from a creator, but through the beginningless cycle of Paticca-samuppada, where phenomena emerge and cease in dependence upon causes and conditions within the vast expanse of Samsara.
From the primordial Brahman, the cosmic vibration of Om manifested the universe, as the creative power of Maya projected the manifold forms of reality from the singular, eternal source of existence.
In the beginning was the Word, and through the Logos, God spoke all things into being, creating the heavens and the earth out of nothing by the power of His divine will.
The All emanated from the Monad through the descent of the Divine Light, as the Primal Mind reflected the archetypal patterns of the cosmos into the material realm of the lower elements.

From the primordial Chaos, the ordering principle of the Logos or the Demiurge imposed form upon matter, establishing the Kosmos as a rational, harmonious structure governed by necessity and divine intelligence.
